quote_original: Not a tree on the outside.

My consciousness, my I AMness is the great tree, and habit once more suggests emptiness, it suggests barrenness, it suggests four months before I can feast. But I cannot wait four months. I give myself this powerful suggestion that never again will I even for a moment relieve that it will take four months to realize my desire. The belief in lack must from this day on be barren and never again reproduce itself in my mind.

quote_original: The Bible states it this way:
context_before: In prayer you are called upon to believe that you possess what your reason and your senses deny. When you pray believe that you have and you shall receive.
context_after: “Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.

source_title: Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea

quote_original: That is what we must do when we pray.
context_before: “But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.” Mark 11:24, 25, 26
context_after: If I hold some thing against another, be it a belief of sickness, poverty , or anything else, I must loose it and let it go, not by using words of denial but by believing him to be what he desires to be. In that way I completely forgive him. I changed my concept of him. I had ought against him and I forgave him Complete forgetfulness is forgiveness. If I do not forget then I have not forgiven.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard

rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: You have no sacrifice to offer.
context_before: Anyone who prays successfully turns within, and appropriates the state sought.
context_after: Do not let anyone tell you that you must struggle and suffer. You need not struggle for the realization of your desire. Read what it says in the Bible.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Desire is the mainspring of action.
context_before: A little practice will convince us that we can, by controlling our imagination, reshape our future in harmony with our desire.
context_after: We could not move a single finger unless we had a desire to move it. No matter what we do, we follow the desire which at the moment dominates our minds. When we break a habit, our desire to break it is greater than our desire to continue the habit.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: There is no absolutely unselfish desire.
context_before: The desires which impel us to action are those which hold our attention. A desire is but an awareness of something we lack and need to make our life more enjoyable. Desires always have some personal gain in view, the greater the anticipated gain, the more intense is the desire.
context_after: Where there is nothing to gain there is no desire, and consequently no action.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: For example, suppose you desire promotion in your office.
context_before: which FOLLOWS the fulfillment of your desire. Also you must feel yourself into the action until it has all the vividness and distinctness of reality.
context_after: Being congratulated would be an event you would encounter following the fulfillment of your desire. Having selected this action as the one you will experience in imagination, immobilize the physical body; and induce a state akin to sleep, a drowsy state, but one in which you are still able to control the direction of your thoughts, a state in which you are attentive without effort. Then visualize a friend standing before you. Put your imaginary hand into his. Feel it to be solid and real, and carry on an imaginary conversation with him in harmony with the action.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea (1968-01-01).

quote_original: Its appearance and disappearance are measurable.
context_before: Time measures my life without employing the three dimensions of length, width and height. There is no such thing as an instantaneous object.
context_after: It endures for a definite length of time. We can measure its life span without using the dimensions of length, width and height. Time is definitely a fourth way of measuring an object.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 5 – Remain Faithful To Your Idea (1968-01-01).
